title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (previous page): X is a curve over Q with divisor D, X' = X \ D, and π1 = π1(X'_{Q̄}). I and J are sets of 'base points': fibre functors, presumably including tangential base points at the cusps. X̃' is the universal pro-cover, and X̃'(I), X̃'(J) are its sets of points over I and J. These are right π1-sets, one π1-torsor per base point. Γ' is an open subgroup of Gal(Q̄/Q), corresponding to a number field K. A partial splitting gives the arithmetic extension 1 → π1 → E'_{Γ'} → Γ' → 1. For γ in Γ', B_γ is the fibre of E' over γ, a π1-bitorsor. γ acts on the Galois category Revét(X') ≃ Ens_f(π1) by E ↦ B_γ ∧_{π1} E.

This page: suppose a finite étale cover Y' corresponds to the finite left π1-set E. Then Y'(I) ≃ X̃'(I) ∧_{π1} E, and likewise for J. The canonical isomorphisms (11), Y'(I) ≃ (^γY')(I), therefore become isomorphisms X̃'(I) ∧ E ≃ (X̃'(I) ∧ B_γ) ∧ E, functorial in E. By the Yoneda/Tannakian argument these come from isomorphisms of right π1-sets X̃'(I) ≃ X̃'(I) ∧_{π1} B_γ. Such isomorphisms are the same as maps B_γ → Bij(X̃'(I), X̃'(I)) that are compatible with π1 acting on both sides (semilinear maps).

Letting γ vary, these maps glue to a single map E'_{Γ'} = ⋃ B_γ → Aut_Ens(X̃'(I)), and likewise for J. Grothendieck observes this is exactly the natural action of the arithmetic fundamental group E' on the fibres of the universal cover at the base points I, J. It extends the π1-action.

So the Galois data on the I-pointed fundamental groupoid is encoded in a single object: the extension E' together with its action on the π1-sets X̃'(I), X̃'(J). The next page uses this to reconstruct the I-fundamental groupoid Π1(X';I) and the Galois action on it. This is part of setting up the 'paradigm' description of the outer/groupoid Galois representation in the Longue Marche/Esquisse programme.
errors: The page does not check that the glued map E' → Aut(X̃'(I)) is multiplicative, i.e. a group action. This needs the cocycle compatibility of the isomorphisms (11) under composition γ, γ'. It follows from the functoriality of the Galois action on covers, but is left implicit.

Left/right conventions are loose. X̃'(I) is a right π1-set, and the maps B_γ → Bij must be semilinear (twisted-equivariant) rather than plain automorphisms of right π1-sets; the phrase 'compatibles avec les op. de π1 à g. et à dr.' covers this only informally. Not a real error.

ideas.what: Fibres of a cover at a set of base points expressed as contracted products: Y'(I) ≃ X̃'(I) ∧_{π1} E.
ideas.modern_name: Fibre functors in a Galois category; contracted product with the universal torsor

ideas.what: The Galois element γ acts on the category of covers through the bitorsor B_γ = fibre of the extension E' over γ.
ideas.modern_name: Outer action via bitorsors; arithmetic fundamental group extension
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX (exact sequence); bitorsor language in Grothendieck/Giraud

ideas.what: The Galois action on fibre functors at several (tangential) base points is equivalent to an action of the arithmetic extension E' on X̃'(I), extending the π1-action. This is a step towards encoding the Galois action on the multi-pointed fundamental groupoid.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on profinite fundamental groupoids with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche); Deligne 1989; Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping translation, from Galois action on covers to action of the extension E' on fibres of the universal cover at a base-point set. It is standard Galois-category/torsor formalism and matches material in La Longue Marche. Nothing new or unexpected.
transcription_corrections: 'isomorphisme (**)' should read 'isomorphisme (11)', referring to (11) on the previous page.
'et item pour' should read 'et idem pour'.
'E'_{Γ'} = ⋃_{γ∈Γ'} B_γ' is correct; the index is Γ', not Γ.
The last lines read roughly: 'et celle qu'on cherche est précisément l'opération déduite par celles déjà envisagée(s) de E' sur X̃'(I), X̃'(J) ...'.
